eyebrow: I³/NYC Research · Company census · Data as of October 11, 2026
title: New York City's AI and physical AI companies

lede.t: A census of 150 companies with their headquarters or primary office in the five boroughs that have raised at least $1M or passed $1M in revenue. Each profile records what the company sells and to whom, whose models it runs on, its funding, scale, footprint in the city and one main use case with impact indicators.

sub.t: Eight findings computed from the profiles below. The census is a curated sample of the city's funded AI companies, not a complete register; see the method notes for what is missing.

caveats.t: Companies whose product is AI or depends on it, with headquarters or primary US office in the five boroughs, and at least $1M raised or $1M in revenue. Three rows (Sola, Cedar, Accrete AI) are included on reported rounds whose amounts could not be confirmed.

The city counts more than 2,000 AI startups. This census profiles 150 of the best funded and most visible. Research ran against a fixed search budget, so many candidates were never checked; 184 names that were reviewed and left out are listed below with the reason.

Seven sector desks built long lists from funding trackers, investor portfolios and press, then verified each company against its own site, filings, and dated coverage. Records were merged, de-duplicated and coded into common categories for cohort analysis.
Company sites and press releases, SEC filings for public companies, AlleyWatch, TechCrunch, Sacra, CB Insights, Built In NYC, Wikipedia and trade press. Each profile links its sources.
34 profiles are rated high, 14 low. Low means the headquarters attribution or the funding figures rest on a single aggregator. Low-confidence rows carry a label.

Only 34 companies have a revenue or ARR figure, and most are company statements or press estimates, not audited. Public companies report under GAAP. Lemonade's figure is the midpoint of its FY2026 guidance; Hume AI's is a projection.
34 companies have no total-raised figure, so sums understate. Valuations are last known and can be years old (Opentrons 2021, Hugging Face 2023).
Coded from what companies and press say. 63 companies disclose nothing usable and are left as undisclosed. Provider counts include only named providers.
32 older platforms that added AI to an existing product (Datadog, MongoDB, UiPath, Taboola and others) are labelled AI-enabled. That label is an analyst judgment; use the lens to exclude them.
A street address or neighborhood was found for 78 companies. District shares apply to those only. New York headcount, as distinct from global headcount, is almost never published.

Aescape is listed as bankrupt by one data provider while its site is live. Darrow and Brightwave have disputed headquarters. General Intuition's latest round and $6.2B valuation come from CB Insights and one press report.
Research closed October 11, 2026. Founding year is missing for 17 companies.

footer.t: , Vice Chair, Board Member & Co-Founder, I³/NYC. Prepared for I³/NYC, the non-profit connecting Italian innovators with New York City. Figures are compiled from public sources and are not investment advice.
